text: Almost 40% of Canada has fewer people
Canada has 10 provinces and three territories.
Yukon, the Northwest Territories, and Nunavut.
but only about 136,000 people live there,
That's roughly one Narendra Modi stadium.
Nunavut alone is about two million square kilometers, almost as big as Mexico. Its capital,
Iqaluit, has no road to any other town. You fly in or arrive by sea when the ice allows.
So why aren't they provinces? Provinces get their powers from Canada's Constitution.
Territories get theirs from Ottawa through ordinary federal laws. Two of them don't even
have political parties. They govern by consensus. And in 2027, Nunavut takes control of its
own land and resources. Still not a province. Still huge.
